T2.basis: the pair has identical current content and different histories; no function of K_t can distinguish them

T5.question: Can an external History context provide it without enlarging the kernel?
T5.basis: zero kernel reads of history; the preservation duty (AX-5, I9) is WRITE-SIDE and is satisfiable by an append-only store outside the kernel

T4.question: Does anything require the EVENT, or merely historical state?
T4.basis: AX-5 / I9 / §17 require the record to SURVIVE. Preservation is not consumption. No operation reads the record, so nothing requires the event qua event.

re-closure under a stronger standard.note: a governance rule of the form 'a reopened proposition needs a stronger standard' would read history. THE THEORY CONTAINS NO SUCH RULE.

stability / churn metric.note: an analytics concern; no theory object consumes it

explanation / why-do-we-believe-X.note: AX-5 provenance preservation and I9 require the trail to SURVIVE; they do not require any OPERATION to read it

supersession traceability (\u00a717 / CE.note: the theory requires a superseded claim to remain traceable — again a PRESERVATION obligation, not an operation input

corpus_search.finding: every hit is either RESEARCH-PROGRAMME closure (steps, audits, gap closure) — a different sense of 'closed' — or the KR-CLOSURE protocol's own scenario text (S14). NO operation, rule or policy in the corpus reads whether a proposition was previously closed.
corpus_search.consequence: Hypothesis B has NO corpus support: it is a design option, not a discovered fact.
